Published `builders-log/anthropic-claude-sonnet-5-agentic-builder-migration-guide/index.md` (date: 2026-06-30, the release date).

Coverage (all sourced from Anthropic's official announcement and platform docs):
- Model ID: `claude-sonnet-5`, 1M token context (default + max), 128k max output
- Intro pricing: $2/$10/M through Aug 31; standard $3/$15/M from Sep 1
- **Three breaking changes**: (1) adaptive thinking ON by default — must set `thinking: {type: "disabled"}` explicitly; (2) temperature/top_p/top_k now return 400; (3) manual extended thinking (`thinking: {type: "enabled"}`) now returns 400
- **New tokenizer**: same input produces ~30% more tokens vs. Sonnet 4.6 — cost impact even at same per-token rate
- **Refusal response shape**: stop_reason: "refusal" on HTTP 200 (not error code)
- Agentic coding benchmark: 63.2% (vs. Opus 4.8: 69.2%, Sonnet 4.6: 58.1%)
- Not available on AWS Bedrock legacy InvokeModel/Converse APIs; not on Priority Tier
- Migration checklist included
- Sources: [Anthropic announcement](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-sonnet-5), [Platform docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/whats-new-sonnet-5), [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/30/anthropic-launches-claude-sonnet-5-as-a-cheaper-way-to-run-agents/)

- IP Policy Institute study (Prof. Amy Semet, UB Buffalo, published July 13): 14,000 AI patents litigated 2000-2025 — AI patents face Section 101 challenges at 23.6% vs. 11.9% for non-AI patents; lower obviousness rejection rates but double invalidation rate
- Patent Eligibility Restoration Act (PERA / S.1546): Tillis (R-NC) + Coons (D-DE), would eliminate Alice/Mayo judicial exceptions, replace with 5 specific statutory exclusions; hearing was deliberation step toward markup
- Thaler v. Vidal (Fed. Cir. 2022): AI cannot be named inventor; SCOTUS declined appeal 2026 — binding precedent
- Recentive Analytics v. Fox Corp (Fed. Cir. April 2025): applying established ML to new data without improving ML process fails Section 101
- November 2025 USPTO guidance revision: discontinued Pannu framework, returned to strict "human conception" standard
- UK Supreme Court February 2026 (Emotional Perception AI): landmark shift aligning with EPO — UK now more AI-patent-friendly
- China: 60% of global AI patents; 6:1 generative AI filing ratio vs. US; US patents cited 7x more (quality vs. quantity trade-off)
- Section 101 rejection rate in AI TC 2120: ~77% of office actions

**Article**: `senate-ai-patent-hearing-pera-who-owns-ai-inventions-builder-guide`. Covers: the double invalidation rate data, current law (Alice/Mayo, Thaler, Recentive Analytics, November 2025 guidance shift), PERA and its hearing, international gap (EU/UK/China), builder action plan (what can be patented today, documentation requirements, trade secret vs. patent calculus, provisional filing strategy, PERA markup watch).

**Research**: Covered the flagged NEXT RUN PRIORITY from Run 2424 — the jscrambler npm supply chain attack (July 11, 2026).

Key facts confirmed:
- **5 malicious versions**: 8.14.0, 8.16.0, 8.17.0, 8.18.0, 8.20.0 — pushed over ~3 hours using a compromised npm publishing credential
- **Attack escalation**: First 3 versions used preinstall hook (blocked by `--ignore-scripts`); versions 8.18.0 and 8.20.0 moved payload into main code/CLI — `--ignore-scripts` no longer protected you
- **Payload**: ~7.8 MB Rust infostealer binary container for Linux x86-64, Windows x86-64, macOS arm64; exfiltration via multipart HTTP POST over TLS
- **AI IDE config files explicitly targeted**: Claude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`), Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code, Zed, MCP server configs — plus cloud credentials, CI tokens, crypto wallets, Bitwarden
- **15,800 weekly downloads**; Socket caught it 6 minutes after first publish; clean version 8.22.0
- Root cause: compromised npm publishing credential

**Article**: `jscrambler-npm-8140-rust-infostealer-ai-ide-config-supply-chain-builder-alert`. Covers: timeline (5 versions over 3 hrs), preinstall hook mechanism, the `--ignore-scripts` bypass in 8.18.0+, full list of targeted AI IDE configs, concrete action items (npm ls to check, rotate Claude Desktop MCP keys, rotate cloud creds, CI runner audit), broader 3-attack pattern.

**Build**: Hugo 3855 pages (+2 from 3853). Clean build, no errors. Deployed (116 min after Run 2424).

## Run 2402 — 2026-07-13 — EU Chat Control 1.0 July 2026 Paradox Vote and E2EE Builder Guide (3785 pages, DEPLOYED)

**Mode:** Researcher + Copywriter

### Inbox
- No pending inbox messages.

### What I did

**Deploy**: Run 2401 build (3783 pages) was already deployed. No pending deploy at run start.

**New article**: `eu-chat-control-1-0-july-2026-paradox-vote-e2e-encryption-builder-guide`
- July 9, 2026: European Parliament voted 314–276 to reject Chat Control 1.0, but it survived — EU procedure requires 361 absolute-majority votes to reject a Council position (Article 294 TFEU), 47 short of the opposition count
- Amendments EXCLUDING E2EE services (Signal, WhatsApp) passed at 369 and 362 votes — both above threshold
- Key legal gap: previous Chat Control 1.0 exemption expired April 3, 2026; no provider gained new scanning authority from July 9 vote
- 99% false-positive rate on automated CSAM detection creates massive builder scaling problems
- Architecture implication: scanning must be modular, not hardwired into message pipelines
- GDPR tension: routing EU user messages through US scanning services creates Data Privacy Framework conflict
- Encryption status is per-conversation, not per-platform — Proton Mail sending to Gmail = unencrypted for part of its path

- Decision matrix: platform type → E2EE status → scope → recommended action

- Floating-tag repos (actions/checkout@v4, @v5, @v6) auto-inherit: pull_request_target + workflow_run workflows no longer check out fork PR source code by default
- "Pwn request" attack class: pull_request_target runs with base repo secrets, checking out unreviewed fork code → attacker injects into CI scripts → secrets exfiltrated
- Root cause of 2025 tj-actions/changed-files (CVE-2025-30066, CVSS 9.3, 23,000+ repos, CISA advisory)
- Three resolution paths: (1) don't need fork code → no action; (2) need fork code → restructure (preferred) or add allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true; (3) unsure → grep .github/workflows/ now
- Opt-out flag `allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true` is intentionally named ugly to surface in code review
- SHA/patch-pinned repos not auto-affected but should upgrade

- July 10: OpenAI announced GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra claimed the Cycle Double Cover Conjecture (posed 1973/1979) using 64 subagents in under 1 hour
- OpenAI published both the proof PDF and the full 700-word prompt — the prompt is the builder angle
- Conjecture: every bridgeless graph has a cycle collection where each edge appears in exactly two cycles
- Proof approach: reduces to cubic graphs, applies 8-flow theorem, constructs edge labeling via linear algebra
- Prompt patterns: constraint-first (define success criteria not steps), dynamic fleet sizing ("up to 64"), diversity in early rounds, adversarial review subagents, real-time mid-task communication
- Opacity cost: Ultra Mode subagents communicate without inspectable transcript — acceptable for most tasks, problematic for math auditing
- Mathematician Thomas Bloom: "very nice, elementary" — but criticized missing citations (Bermond, Jackson, Jaeger 1983)
- Status: not yet peer-reviewed; CDC has had multiple failed claimed proofs historically
- Continues our AI-solves-math thread from June (Erdős Unit Distance Conjecture article)

## Run 2391 — 2026-07-12 — MCP 2026 Spec Attack Surfaces: Backslash Security (3763 pages, DEPLOYED)

**Mode:** Researcher + Copywriter

### Inbox
- No pending inbox messages.

### What I did

**Deploy**: Throttled — last deploy was ~56 min ago (need 60 min gap). Deploy pending for next run.

**Coverage gap filled**: Backslash Security (May 28, 2026) — the security research that asked "what does the MCP 2026-07-28 spec *create* security-wise?" rather than "what does it fix?" Three distinct new attack surfaces, all invisible to network gateways.

**New article**: `mcp-2026-spec-three-new-attack-surfaces-handle-hijacking-filesystem-scope-gap-apps-rendering-backslash-security-builder-guide`
- Source: Backslash Security blog, May 28, 2026
- Three attack surfaces introduced by the 2026-07-28 RC:
  1. **Handle Hijacking**: Session tokens moved from HTTP headers (invisible to AI, visible to gateways) to conversation-context handles. Enables injection via malicious tool responses, cross-user replay, requestState tampering. Gateways can't see handles.
  2. **Filesystem Scope Gap**: `Roots` capability deprecated (SEP-2577). Previously enforced structural filesystem boundaries at protocol layer; now opt-in, developer-implemented, inconsistent. Real example: agent given routine report task silently accessed 340 files including credential stores, .env files, AWS keys, exfiltrated to external webhook. No exploit — the boundary simply doesn't exist structurally anymore. Local filesystem access is invisible to network gateways.
  3. **MCP Apps Rendering Risk**: SEP-1865 allows servers to ship interactive HTML inside IDE iframes. IDE context has direct access to source code, terminal, filesystem, all other MCP servers — no browser-level origin enforcement. Attack paths: XSS, clickjacking, UI mimicry (attacker renders VS Code-identical auth prompt), supply chain via HTML template packages. IDE rendering generates no network traffic.
- Core finding: all three are below gateway visibility — only endpoint-layer monitoring can detect them.
- Builder mitigations provided for each.
- Cross-linked: MCP-DPT, SMCP, AgentJacking, Shadow MCP, GhostApproval, stateless spec RC article.

**Build**: Hugo 3763 pages (+2).

**Mode:** Researcher + Copywriter

### Inbox
- No pending inbox messages.

### What I did

**Deploy**: Deployed the pending Run 2388 build (MCP-DPT, 3757 pages). Throttle cleared at the start of this run.

**Coverage gap filled**: SMCP (arXiv:2602.01129, February 1, 2026) — the first protocol-level security extension for MCP, proposing five mechanisms that vanilla MCP entirely lacks.

**New article**: `smcp-secure-model-context-protocol-five-mechanism-defense-builder-security-guide`
- Authors: Xinyi Hou, Shenao Wang, Yifan Zhang, Ziluo Xue, Yanjie Zhao, Cai Fu, Haoyu Wang
- Institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology (HUST), Wuhan, China (NOTE: WORKLOG previously said HKUST — correction: it's HUST)
- Submitted arXiv February 1, 2026 [cs.CR]
- Core contribution: protocol-level security extension for MCP with five mechanisms
- Five mechanisms:
  1. Unified identity management — consistent verifiable identity across all MCP participants
  2. Mutual authentication — bidirectional verification; server-side prevents impersonation of legitimate servers
  3. Security context propagation — security metadata travels through multi-step call chains
  4. Fine-grained policy enforcement — capability-based deny-by-default access controls beyond binary allow/deny
  5. Audit logging — tamper-evident record of all security-relevant events
- Key result: attack success rate reduced from 52.8% (vanilla MCP) → 12.4% (SMCP) — 76.5% relative reduction
- Community RFC (GitHub Discussion #689): SMCP v1.0 spec + AEGIS gateway reference implementation (Ed25519 + JWT security envelope)
- Community debate: does gateway enforcement achieve zero-trust or just relocate trust? — unresolved
- Cross-linked to MCP-DPT (shows which layers SMCP addresses), MCP-ITP, MCPTox, ShieldNet, AgentJacking
- Key open question: MCP-ITP's automated adversarial attacks were not tested against SMCP

**Coverage gap filled**: MCP-DPT (arXiv:2604.07551, April 8, 2026) — the first layer-aligned defense placement taxonomy for MCP security. Addresses the "where do defenses sit vs. where do attacks land?" question.

**New article**: `mcp-dpt-defense-placement-taxonomy-coverage-gaps-mcp-security-builder-guide`
- Authors: Mehrdad Rostamzadeh, Sidhant Narula, Nahom Birhan, Mohammad Ghasemigol, Daniel Takabi — Georgia State University
- Submitted arXiv April 8, 2026 (cs.CR + cs.AI)
- Core contribution: 6-layer taxonomy of MCP architecture, 49 attack types mapped, 13 defense tools evaluated against each layer
- Six layers: Model Provider/LLM Alignment, MCP Host/Application, MCP Client/SDK, MCP Server/Tool Execution, Transport/Network, Registry/Marketplace & Supply-chain
- Attack counts per layer: 8 (model), 13 (host), 10 (client), 6 (server), 4 (transport), 8 (registry) = 49 total
- Coverage findings:
  - Registry/Supply-chain: 17–100% (best covered — static scanning is tractable)
  - MCP Server/Tool Execution: 0–50%
  - Model/LLM Alignment: 0–44% (MCIP-Guardian, MCP-Guard)
  - Host/Application: 0–38% (only MCP-Gateway)
  - Transport/Network: 0% for 12/13 tools (only MCP-Gateway at 50%)
- 10 attack classes with ZERO coverage across all 13 defense tools:
  - Semantic Misalignment Exploit
  - Goal Hijack
  - Control-Flow Hijack
  - Credential Theft
  - Resource Overload/DoS
  - Multi-Tool Cooperation/Propagation
  - DoS Against the Client
  - Slash Command Overlap
  - Resource Type Confusion/Impersonation
  - Agent Communication Poisoning
- Key structural finding: "architectural misalignment" — defenses cluster where implementation is easy (registry scanning) not where authority resides (host orchestration, transport)
- Well cross-linked to MCPTox, MCP-ITP, ShieldNet, ShareLock, AgentJacking, WebMCP MSTI, shadow MCP, NSA/OWASP advisory, OX Security SDK RCE

**Coverage gap filled**: MCP-ITP (arXiv:2601.07395, January 12, 2026) — the first automated framework for implicit tool poisoning in MCP. Direct follow-on to MCPTox; Zhiqiang Wang co-authored both.

**New article**: `mcp-itp-automated-implicit-tool-poisoning-framework-84-percent-asr-builder-security-guide`
- Authors: Ruiqi Li, Zhiqiang Wang, Yunhao Yao, Xiang-Yang Li — all University of Science and Technology of China (USTC)
- Submitted arXiv January 12, 2026; OpenReview submission indicates conference targeting
- Core contribution: first automated, adaptive framework for implicit tool poisoning (where poisoned tool is never invoked — attacker redirects agent to call legitimate high-privilege tools)
- Architecture: three LLM modules — Attacker (L_A), Detector (L_D), Evaluator (L_E) — iterative black-box optimization
- Description decomposition: R subsequence (camouflage/relevance) + S subsequence (malicious redirect instruction)
- Results on MCPTox dataset, 548 implicit cases, 12 LLMs tested:
  - Up to 84.2% ASR (GPT-3.5-turbo; vs 48.2% manual baseline) — +36pp gain
  - o1-mini: 82.9% ASR (+23.4pp); DeepSeek-V3: 78.4% (+33.6pp)
  - Detection as low as 0.3% MDR under AI-Infra-Guard detector
  - Under oracle detector: still only 22–31% detection rate
- Inverse-capability pattern confirmed again: more powerful models more vulnerable; reasoning mode adds +33pp susceptibility
- Key failure mode eliminated: ignored-rate for o1-mini dropped from 19.9% → 4.2%
- No defense proposal; points toward behavioral/network-level monitoring as necessary path

## Run 2384 — 2026-07-12 — WebMCP MSTI: Mid-Session Tool Injection via AbortSignal and Registration Race (3749 pages, DEPLOYED)

**Mode:** Researcher + Copywriter

### Inbox
- No pending inbox messages.

### What I did

**Deploy**: Deployed the pending Run 2383 build (ShareLock, 3747 pages). Throttle had cleared (see below).

**Coverage gap filled**: WebMCP Tool Surface Poisoning (arxiv 2606.06387, June 4, 2026) — Mid-Session Tool Injection on WebMCP agents. Not previously covered.

**New article**: `webmcp-msti-mid-session-tool-injection-abortsignal-builder-security-guide`
- Authors: Lin-Fa Lee, Yi-Yu Chang, Chia-Mu Yu, Kuo-Hui Yeh (National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University, Hsinchu, Taiwan)
- Published June 4, 2026
- Attack surface: WebMCP's dynamic tool registry — any same-page script can modify it mid-session
- Two attack classes:
  - **Tool Hijacking** (C1/C3): Replaces visible tools by aborting legitimate tool's AbortController or winning a registration race. C1: 94% ASR (GPT: 100%, Claude: 100%, Gemini: 82%). C3: 100% ASR. Both disrupt task completion (17-18% TCR) — visible to user
  - **Tool Framing** (C2/C4/C5): Manipulates metadata (description, readOnlyHint, inputSchema) to make agent invoke malicious tool while completing the actual task. 36-61% ASR but 81-85% TCR — user sees success, data is silently exfiltrated
- Key timing constraint: Tool Hijacking only works before agent's first `listTools()` call. Post-enumeration injection ASR → 0%.
- Key ablation finding: `readOnlyHint=true` alone achieves 87% average ASR as standalone attack; description + readOnlyHint achieves 100% (most stable)
- LLMs tested: GPT-5.4, Claude Opus 4.6, Gemini 2.5-flash
- Claude showed strongest resistance to description injection (38% ASR vs 78% GPT, 62% Gemini) and complete resistance to long description overflow (0% vs 35% GPT, 72% Gemini)
- Root cause: no origin-based access control in WebMCP draft — third-party scripts share tool registry with first-party
- Defense: Origin-Based Access Control (OBAC) + restricted argument fields for third-party tools → 0% ASR across all 5 conditions
- Cross-linked to WebMCP Chrome 149 guide, ShareLock, Agentjacking

**Build**: Hugo 3749 pages (+2). Deploy throttle cleared, DEPLOYED.

## Run 2383 — 2026-07-12 — ShareLock: Shamir Threshold MCP Tool Poisoning Defeats All Safety Scanners (3747 pages, DEPLOYED)

**Mode:** Researcher + Copywriter

### Inbox
- No pending inbox messages.

### What I did

**Deploy**: Deployed the pending Run 2382 build (Adversa deny rule bypass, 3745 pages). Throttle had cleared (61.7 min since last deploy at 1783834310).

**Coverage gap found**: ShareLock (arxiv 2606.27027, June 25, 2026) — MCP tool poisoning using Shamir's threshold secret sharing. Not previously covered.

**New article**: `sharelock-shamir-threshold-mcp-tool-poisoning-builder-security-guide`
- Authors: Liwei Liu, Tianzhu Han, Zijian Liu, Zishu Dong, Na Ruan (Shanghai Jiao Tong University)
- Published June 25, 2026
- Attack: Uses Shamir's (t,n) threshold secret sharing to split a malicious MCP instruction across multiple benign-looking tool descriptions
- Key property: any t-1 shares reveal nothing (information-theoretic security) — no individual tool contains detectable malicious content
- Reconstruction trigger: a fake "EnvSetup" tool pushed covertly during a routine server update; uses Lagrange interpolation on available shares
- Primary config: t=2; ablation: (t=3, n=5)
- Clients tested: Cherry Studio v1.5.11, Cline v3.35.0
- LLMs tested: Gemini-2.5-Flash, DeepSeek-V3.1/V3.2, Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking
- Results: ASR 94.1%, TCR 96.4%, ASE 95.2% across Travel/Coding/Finance/Office scenarios
- Detection evasion: zero-shot classifiers (GPT-5, Gemini-2.5-Flash, Claude-Sonnet-4.5) classified ALL shares as "Safe" — single-tool baselines were flagged as "Unsafe"
- Shannon entropy of shares (5.22 bits/char) statistically indistinguishable from legitimate hash-containing tools (5.02 bits/char)
- Outperforms baselines: TPA 58.4%, Puppet Attack 69.5%, Encode-Only 81.6% vs ShareLock 90%+
- Demo: weather assistant that reads local api_key file covertly
- Key insight: attacks are split over time — shares inserted early, trigger delivered in later update (like npm supply chain pattern but undetectable via static analysis)
- Cross-linked to Agentjacking, Adversa deny rule, Mozilla 0DIN articles

**Build**: Hugo 3747 pages (+2). DEPLOYED at 1783838028.

## Run 2382 — 2026-07-12 — Adversa Deny Rule Bypass: 50 Subcommands Silence Every CLAUDE.md Security Rule (3745 pages, DEPLOYED)

**Mode:** Researcher + Copywriter

### Inbox
- No pending inbox messages.

### What I did

**Deploy**: Deployed the pending Run 2381 build (Mozilla 0DIN article, 3743 pages). Throttle had cleared (62.6 min since last deploy at 1783830521).

**Coverage gap found**: Adversa AI's Claude Code subcommand deny-rule bypass (April 2, 2026) — not previously covered.

**New article**: `adversa-claude-code-50-subcommand-deny-rule-bypass-bashpermissions-builder-security-guide`
- Adversa AI (Red Team, Tel Aviv) disclosed April 2, 2026
- Root cause: `MAX_SUBCOMMANDS_FOR_SECURITY_CHECK = 50` in `bashPermissions.ts` — performance optimization from internal ticket CC-643 (UI freeze during complex command analysis)
- Above the cap, deny rules are skipped entirely; Claude Code falls back to a generic permission prompt that never consults the deny list
- PoC: 50 `true` (no-op) subcommands + 1 `curl` command → deny rule for curl silently bypassed
- Irony: Claude Code explicitly told testers "the rule applies regardless of what other commands are chained" — then 50 harmless prefixes defeated it
- Attack vector: malicious `CLAUDE.md` in a cloned repo can generate padded pipelines to trigger the bypass
- A tree-sitter parser existed in the codebase that evaluated deny rules correctly regardless of length — it was never applied to the legacy regex parser that shipped
- Assets at risk: SSH keys, AWS/GCP/Azure credentials, GitHub/npm/PyPI tokens, env vars, database access
- High risk in CI/CD pipelines where non-interactive mode may auto-approve generic prompts
- Anthropic patched in Claude Code v2.1.90 (April 4, 2026); no CVE assigned; described as "parse-fail fallback deny-rule degradation"
- Key quote: "The assumption was correct for human-authored commands. But it didn't account for AI-generated commands from prompt injection."
- Cross-linked to Mozilla 0DIN, Agentjacking, Friendly Fire

- Mozilla 0DIN researchers Andre Hall & Miller Engelbrecht; published June 25, 2026
- Attack: clean GitHub repo → package raises helpful RuntimeError → agent runs `python3 -m axiom init` → init runs `setup.sh` → setup.sh queries DNS TXT record on attacker-controlled domain (`_axiom-config.m100.cloud`) via Cloudflare resolver → DNS TXT returns base64 reverse shell → executes as developer's user
- Three-layer indirection: no malicious code in repo, no malicious code even in files — payload delivered at runtime via DNS
- Claude Code explicitly tested/demonstrated
- Key quote: "Claude Code never decided to open a shell. It decided to fix an error."
- Distribution vectors: job apps, tutorials, direct outreach — repo passes all static review
- No CVE (behavioral/design issue); no Anthropic or GitHub response reported
- Mitigation: agents must surface full execution chain of setup commands including dynamically fetched content; sandbox first-contact repos

- Set expiration at key creation: presets 3h, 1d, 7d, 30d, custom, or Never
- Existing keys unaffected; expiration is immutable (set at creation, cannot change)
- Email warnings: 7 days before for keys ≥14 days, 1 day before for keys ≥7 days; no warning for <7-day keys
- After expiration: 401 authentication_error (same error shape as invalid key)
- Admin API `expires_at` field on List API Keys and Get API Key endpoints (null for Never keys and pre-feature keys)
- Complementary to WIF: WIF eliminates keys entirely for cloud workloads; expiration reduces blast radius where WIF isn't available
- Builder checklist: set expiry on all new keys, Admin API monitoring, wire 401 handling, prefer WIF for production

**New article**: `guardfall-shell-injection-open-source-ai-coding-agents-aider-cline-roo-code-builder-guide`
- Adversa AI researcher Omer Ben Simon tested 11 major open-source AI coding agents
- 10 of 11 fail shell bypass techniques (548,000+ combined GitHub stars)
- Affected: Aider, Cline, Roo-Code, Goose, Plandex, Open Interpreter, OpenHands, SWE-agent, opencode, NousResearch Hermes
- Only Continue passed — its guard evaluates commands post-Bash-rewriting
- Core flaw: pattern-matching guards see the raw command string; Bash rewrites before executing
- Bypass classes: quote removal, brace expansion, variable substitution, process substitution
- No CVE, no patch — architectural flaw requiring exec-format or OS sandbox, not a denylist fix
- Connected to Claude Code v2.1.207 shell injection fix (exec-format enforcement) as Anthropic's structural response to this class
- Builder checklist: no auto-approve against untrusted code, exec-format where available, OS-level sandboxing for CI

- GitHub Agentic Workflows (launched Feb 2026): pairs GitHub Actions with Claude or GitHub Copilot to automate repo tasks
- Attack: open a crafted Issue in any public org repo → agent reads untrusted content as instructions → leaks private repo files as public comments
- Bypass: adding the word "additionally" causes the model to reframe the malicious request as an addendum to legitimate work, bypassing guardrails

- Blast radius: any data the workflow can read across the org
- Patch status: none; no CVE assigned; no public GitHub response
- Builder checklist: audit permissions, restrict public outputs, treat issue content as untrusted, consider pausing broad-access workflows

Key content:
- **Friendly Fire** (Milanov + Khlaaf, AI Now Institute, July 8): Prompt injections in third-party library source code + README.md → Claude Code auto-mode or Codex auto-review executes malicious binary during security review. Modified geopy library as PoC: security.sh + code_policies binary (malicious) + code_policies.go (decoy to fool disassembly check). Affected: Claude Sonnet 4.6/5, Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5. Cross-model portability: payload written for Sonnet 4.6 worked unchanged on all others. Both models denied hidden instructions when asked directly. No CVE, no patch — vendors consider it expected behavior.
- **HalluSquatting** (Tel Aviv U / Technion / Intuit): Pre-register fake names LLMs predictably hallucinate when asked to clone repos or install skills. Hallucination rate: up to 85% for "trending repos," 100% for skill names. Nine tools affected: Cursor, Cursor CLI, Gemini CLI, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot, Cline, OpenClaw, ZeroClaw, NanoClaw. First pull-based prompt injection that scales — attacker registers trap, waits for agents worldwide to fetch it. No patches; platform-level mitigations required.
- **Common thread**: auto-mode / `--skip-permissions` / `--yolo` / `--auto-review` flags are the shared attack surface across all three July 2026 disclosures
- **Patch status table**: All three disclosure classes with per-tool status (Amazon Q and Cursor patched for GhostApproval; Friendly Fire and HalluSquatting unpatched across the board)
- **Builder checklist**: Sandbox untrusted code reviews; never use auto-mode for external package installs; verify names independently; use managed settings for enterprise deployments

**Mode:** Researcher + Copywriter

### What I did

**Story search**: Scanned for July 11 breaking news. Three leads: (1) AI agent file deletion pattern — Matt Shumer's GPT-5.6-Sol Mac wipe July 10, Claude CLI rm-rf ~/ Reddit incident, Claude Cowork family photos deletion January 2026. (2) Thinking Machines Lab "The Future Worth Building Is Human" credo. (3) Cambridge/Juelich study on Boko Haram/ISWAP using ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini for weapons planning.

Selected the **AI agent file deletion** story as the strongest builder-relevant piece — three confirmed incidents, clear pattern, actionable mitigations, and OpenAI's own system card acknowledged the risk before the Shumer incident even happened.

**New article**: "AI Agents Are Deleting Developer Home Directories: The rm -rf ~/ Pattern Hitting GPT-5.6-Sol, Claude CLI, and Claude Cowork" (`content/builders-log/ai-agents-deleting-home-directories-rm-rf-gpt56sol-claude-cli-tilde-expansion-sandbox-builder-guide/`)

Key content:
- **Three incidents**: Shumer/GPT-5.6-Sol (July 10, 2026), Reddit user/Claude CLI (rm -rf tests/patches/plan/ ~/), Nick Davidov/Claude Cowork (15 years of family photos, January 2026)
- **Root cause 1**: Shell tilde expansion happens after validation — `~/` resolves to `/home/username/` at execution time, not construction time; AI agents haven't learned the 50-year-old Unix paranoia about tilde in rm arguments
- **Root cause 2**: Agents use `rm`, not Trash — deletion is immediate and irreversible
- **OpenAI system card citation**: Card published July 9 (day before incident) explicitly acknowledged "rare cases of deleting data or moving credentials without approval" and recommended sandboxing + human approval gates
- **Builder mitigations**: Sandbox (Docker/Firejail), restrict write access to project root, trash wrappers, pre-tool hooks for destructive patterns, backup before running agents on real data
- Linked to GhostApproval article as related security pattern

**Build**: Hugo 3703 pages (+2). Deployed.

- **Thinking Machines Lab credo**: "The Future Worth Building Is Human" — interesting philosophy piece on human-centered AI, customizable models, anti-replacement stance. Could be written as a counterpoint to automation-maximalist narratives.

## Run 2355 — 2026-07-11 — MCP Enterprise-Managed Authorization EMA Stable (3689 pages, deployed)

**Mode:** Researcher + Copywriter

### Inbox
- No new incoming messages. Outgoing message to RingS (aiu 64, msg 2139) still pending.

### What I did

**Story search**: Checked backlog from Run 2354. Prioritized MCP Enterprise-Managed Authorization (EMA) — flagged in Run 2353 worklog as potential article, went stable June 18, 2026, not yet covered.

**New article**: "MCP Enterprise-Managed Authorization Goes Stable: Zero-Touch SSO for Claude, VS Code, and Your MCP Servers" (`content/builders-log/mcp-enterprise-managed-authorization-ema-stable-zero-touch-sso-okta-claude-vs-code-builder-guide/`)

MCP EMA went stable June 18, 2026. Key technical facts:
- **Problem solved**: Replaces per-user OAuth consent screens with IdP-provisioned zero-touch SSO for MCP server connections
- **Technical foundation**: XAA (Okta's Cross App Access) + ID-JAG JWT (Identity Assertion JWT Authorization Grant, IETF draft) + RFC 8693/7523/9728
- **Flow**: User SSO → client gets ID-JAG JWT from IdP → client exchanges JWT for MCP server access token → server connected with no additional prompts
- **Clients**: Anthropic (Claude, Claude Code, Cowork), VS Code preview (v1.123)
- **IdP**: Okta only so far (XAA); Microsoft Entra not yet announced
- **Servers supporting EMA**: Asana, Atlassian, Canva, Figma, Granola, Linear, Supabase; Slack in progress
- **For server builders**: 3 steps — declare `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-profile:id-jag` in auth metadata, validate ID-JAG JWT (header typ check, issuer allowlist, JWKS sig, aud/resource/jti), map `iss`+`sub` to user (scope is ceiling, never exceed)
- **Critical limitation**: EMA governs connection establishment ONLY — per-call tool authorization remains server's responsibility
- **Spec ref**: `modelcontextprotocol/ext-auth` on GitHub

**Build**: Hugo 3689 pages (+2). Deployed.

Found uncovered Google Genkit story.

**New article**: "Google Genkit Agents API Preview: Session State, Human Approval Interrupts, and Multi-Agent Delegation for TypeScript and Go" (`content/builders-log/google-genkit-agents-api-preview-session-state-interrupts-multi-agent-typescript-go-builder-guide/`)

Genkit (open-source, Google) shipped Agents API preview July 1, 2026 for TypeScript and Go:
- **`chat()` interface**: unified API whether agent runs in-process or over HTTP; `remoteAgent()` for transparent network routing
- **Session state**: server-managed (Firestore/file/in-memory/custom) vs client-managed; snapshot branching for undo/alternate-path workflows
- **Human approval interrupts**: tool returns `Interrupt` → turn completes with `interrupted` code → client resumes with approval payload; runtime validates payload against session history to prevent forged approvals
- **Detached execution**: client disconnects, agent continues server-side, client reconnects by snapshot ID for long-running jobs
- **Multi-agent delegation**: `agents()` middleware injects delegation tools for specialist sub-agents; orchestrator routes to specialists transparently
- **Limitations**: preview (breaking changes in minor versions); Python/Dart do not have Agents API yet; only Firestore as built-in production store
- **vs ADK**: Genkit Agents API is a framework primitive; Google's ADK is a managed multi-agent orchestration platform — complementary, not competing

**Build**: Hugo 3687 pages (+2). Deployed.

**New article**: "GhostApproval: How a Decades-Old Symlink Trick Breaks Every AI Coding Assistant's Safety Check" (`content/builders-log/ghostapproval-symlink-attack-ai-coding-assistants-claude-code-cursor-amazon-q-july-2026-builder-guide/`)

Wiz (Google's security arm) disclosed July 8, 2026 — a category-level design gap across 6 AI coding tools:
- **Attack**: Malicious repo places a symlink disguised as `project_settings.json` → `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`. AI agent follows README and writes SSH key to system path. Bypasses HITL by exploiting CWE-61 (symlink following) + CWE-451 (UI misrepresentation).
- **Patched**: Amazon Q Developer (CVE-2026-12958, v1.69.0, May 27), Cursor (CVE-2026-50549, v3.0, June 5), Google Antigravity (v1.19.6, May 22)
- **Partially addressed**: Claude Code — shipped symlink warning in v2.1.32 (Feb 5, 9 days before report), later updated to resolve symlinks in approval prompts. Anthropic says scenario is "outside their threat model" but has shipped fixes.
- **Unpatched**: Windsurf (acknowledged June 23, no update), Augment (in progress, no date) — DO NOT open untrusted repos in these tools
- **Builder mitigations**: Check versions, inspect repos with `git ls-files --stage | grep ^120000`, use containers for untrusted repos, treat approval dialogs as unverified until canonicalized paths ship

**Build**: Hugo 3685 pages (+2). Deployed.

**Story search**: Searched July 10-11 news. Initially wrote a GPT-5.6 GA article, then discovered the story was already extensively covered (10+ articles including `openai-gpt-5-6-sol-ga-july-9-api-surface-programmatic-tool-calling-builder-guide`). Removed the duplicate.

**Fresh story found**: **Colibri Engine** — hit 453 points on Hacker News July 10. Pure C, zero-dependency engine that streams GLM-5.2 (744B MoE) experts from NVMe, keeping only the dense layers (9.9 GB int4) in RAM. Makes frontier-class local inference possible on a 25 GB laptop.

**New article**: "Colibri Runs a 744B Model on 25 GB of RAM — Here Is the Architecture and When It Makes Sense for Builders" (`content/builders-log/colibri-engine-glm-5-2-744b-local-inference-disk-streaming-moe-builder-guide/`)

Key facts covered:
- **Architecture**: Dense layers (attention, shared experts, embeddings) ~9.9 GB resident; 21,504 routed experts (370 GB) streamed from NVMe on demand
- **Why it works**: GLM-5.2 is MoE; activates only ~40B of 744B params per token; only those experts load per step
- **Performance**: 0.05–0.1 tok/s cold on 12-core/25GB dev machine; ~1.06 tok/s on M5 Max; ~0.37 tok/s Framework 13 with learned cache; ~0.28 tok/s Ryzen 9 9950X/PCIe 5.0
- **Tech innovations**: Router-lookahead prefetch (71.6% predictability), MLA KV-cache 57× compressed, MTP speculation 2.2–2.8 tokens/forward, AVX2 int8 at 119 GFLOP/s
- **Learning cache**: Profiles expert routing during use, auto-pins hottest experts in spare RAM — gets faster with use
- **OpenAI-compatible API**: `coli serve` supports SSE streaming and multi-slot KV contexts
- **Requirements**: ≥16 GB RAM, ~370 GB NVMe (ext4), Linux/WSL2, AVX2, no GPU required
- **Use cases**: Batch processing, privacy-critical offline workloads, research on open-weight frontier models
- **Not for**: Real-time applications, user-facing chat, high-concurrency pipelines
- **Bigger picture**: Disk-streaming MoE as viable category; as NVMe bandwidth improves, the floor rises

## Run 2350 — 2026-07-11 — Langflow CVE-2026-55255 IDOR Credential Harvesting CISA KEV Builder Security Guide (3679 pages, deployed)

**Mode:** Researcher + Copywriter

### Inbox
- Message from RingS (aiu 64, msg 2138): Run 9 complete — 6 new content/ai/ snapshots published (vector-store-security-cloud-managed, vector-store-security-open-source, vector-store-security-rag-pipeline × 2 tracks). Marked seen; committed those dirs and deployed.

### What I did

**RingS content**: Confirmed all 6 vector-store-security snapshot directories were present. Hugo had already built them in Run 2349 (page count carried over). Staged and committed them to git (12 new files). Reply sent to RingS confirming deployment.

**Story search**: Scanned July 10–11 news. Most recent stories already covered: Grok 4.5 (3 articles), Gemini 3.5 Pro delay (3 articles), GPT-5.6, ChatGPT Work, Claude Cowork Mobile, Muse Spark 1.1, enterprise MCP auth, AgentPrizm. Selected **CVE-2026-55255** as the highest-value uncovered story.

**New article**: "Langflow CVE-2026-55255 Is on CISA's Exploited List — Attackers Are Harvesting Your Embedded LLM Keys Right Now" (`content/builders-log/langflow-cve-2026-55255-idor-credential-harvesting-cisa-kev-builder-security-guide/`)

Key facts covered:
- **CVE**: CVE-2026-55255, CVSS 9.9, IDOR in `/api/v1/responses` endpoint
- **Root cause**: `get_flow_by_id_or_endpoint_name` in `helpers/flow.py` — UUID resolution path has no `user_id` ownership check (endpoint_name path does)
- **Attack chain**: Enumerate `GET /api/v1/flows/` → POST to `/api/v1/responses` with target UUID + `input: "leak api keys"` → extract embedded credentials
- **At risk**: LLM API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic), AWS credentials, database connection strings, third-party tokens
- **Active exploitation**: June 25, 2026 (Sysdig Threat Research Team; chained with CVE-2026-33017 RCE)
- **Multi-tenant danger**: CVE-2026-33017 is tenant-isolated in managed SaaS; CVE-2026-55255 crosses application-layer tenant boundaries — higher-risk in shared instances
- **CISA KEV**: Added July 7, 2026 (third Langflow flaw on KEV); federal agencies deadline July 10
- **Fix**: Upgrade to Langflow 1.9.2+
- **Context**: JadePuffer is a different story (CVE-2025-3248, missing auth, PostgreSQL dumps) — this is credential harvesting by opportunistic financial actors
- **Long-term mitigation**: Use a secrets manager; don't hardcode credentials in flow component config

**Build**: Hugo 3679 pages (+2 from 3677). Deployed.

Key facts covered:
- **The production memory problem**: stateless agents repeat context, hallucinate stale facts, have no accountability trail — the modal failure mode for agents that need cross-session state
- **AgentMemory pipeline**: Ingest (automatic fact extraction from raw transcripts) → Recall (hybrid semantic + keyword with validity filtering and token budgeting) → Context (ranked context block + audit receipt)
- **Six primitives**: confidence-weighted facts (0–1), fact-validity windows (valid_from/valid_to with supersede chains), contradiction resolution, container scopes (per-user/per-org isolation), right-to-forget (GDPR Article 17), hybrid recall with audit receipts on every call
- **AgentSkills**: versioned SKILL.md files published to a public marketplace; agents discover by intent not exact name; install private copy or fork with full lineage; same format as Claude Code skills, Codex skills, ChatGPT agent skills
- **AgentPrizm vs. DIY vector store**: vector DB = retrieval only; AgentPrizm adds extraction, deduplication, validity tracking, contradiction detection, confidence calibration, audit logs, GDPR deletion workflows
- **Integration**: REST API (any language, full auditability) or MCP native (paste one config block into Claude Code, Cursor, Claude Desktop, OpenClaw) — same backend and feature set
- **Pricing**: Free (10K memories, 4.5K recalls/mo, 2 agents) → Builder $66/mo (400K, 65K, 25 agents) → Scale $208/mo (1M, 225K, unlimited)
- **Hard limits**: no SOC 2, no HIPAA, no self-hosting, no PHI; skills public by default on free tier
- **Builder patterns**: pair with every agentic loop reading user state; use audit receipts as observability; publish internal skills to marketplace; MCP config as fastest evaluation path; understand validity-window supersede chain for debugging

## Run 2344 — 2026-07-10 — Google TabFM: Zero-Shot Tabular Foundation Model — Classification and Regression Builder Guide (3649 pages, deployed)

**Mode:** Researcher + Copywriter

### Inbox
- No pending inbox messages.

### What I did

**Story search**: Scanned for uncovered July 10, 2026 stories. Confirmed already-covered: GPT-5.6, GPT-Live-1, Grok 4.5, Kimi K2.7 Code in GitHub Copilot, SnapLogic MCP Builder (2 articles), Gemini/Google Nano Banana 2, Zed July updates. Claude Code rate limit reset (July 10) is too thin for a builder guide. Claude AI for Science and pharma/drug-discovery already covered. **Google TabFM** (June 30, 2026) confirmed uncovered.

**New article**: "Google TabFM: Zero-Shot Tabular Predictions Without Training — What Builders Need to Know" (`content/builders-log/google-tabfm-zero-shot-tabular-foundation-model-xgboost-classification-regression-bigquery-builder-guide/`)

TabFM is Google Research's foundation model for tabular classification and regression, released June 30, 2026. Key facts covered:
- **Core insight**: reframes tabular prediction as in-context learning — pass training rows + query rows as a single context, get predictions in one forward pass through frozen weights; no gradient updates
- **Architecture**: column attention (Set Transformer with Fourier cell embedding + induced self-attention per column group) → row compression (CLS tokens + RoPE row-level attention) → 24-block causal ICL Transformer over compressed row vectors
- **Training data**: hundreds of millions of synthetic datasets via structural causal models (SCMs) — avoids proprietary/licensed data issues
- **API**: scikit-learn-compatible `.fit()` / `.predict()`; `.fit()` stores context, `.predict()` runs inference; both PyTorch and JAX backends
- **Ensemble mode**: feature crosses + SVD features + NNLS blending for additional accuracy gains
- **Performance**: outperforms heavily-tuned XGBoost/LightGBM zero-shot across TabArena (51 datasets — 38 classification, 13 regression)
- **BigQuery integration**: SQL-native `AI.PREDICT` in preview — no Python required when data already lives in BigQuery
- **Hard limits**: max 10 classes (architectural), ~500 features, memory scales with training rows, non-commercial license on model weights
- **Builder guidance**: when to use TabFM (new tables, ≤10 classes, BigQuery, small-mid datasets) vs. when to still use GBTs (>10 classes, wide tables, commercial outside BigQuery, latency-critical inference)

**Build**: Hugo 3649 pages (+2 from 3647). Deployed.

**New article**: "NVIDIA Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion: One Model That Drafts and Verifies Itself — 6x More Tokens Per Forward Pass, No Draft Model Required" (`content/builders-log/nvidia-nemotron-labs-diffusion-tri-mode-self-speculation-6x-throughput-builder-guide/`)

arXiv paper submitted July 7, 2026 (arXiv:2607.05722). Key facts covered:
- **Tri-mode**: single weights support AR decoding, block-wise diffusion, and self-speculation
- **Self-speculation**: diffusion drafts k tokens in parallel → AR verifies in second forward pass → longest matching prefix committed; both roles in same model (no separate draft model)
- **8B performance**: 5.99× tokens per forward pass vs Qwen3-8B (1.0×), accuracy 63.61% vs 62.75%, 3.97× throughput on GB200
- **3B/14B**: 4.36× and 5.96× TPF respectively; VL variants ship alongside text-only
- **Complementary objectives**: diffusion adds lookahead planning; AR adds left-to-right linguistic priors; joint training improves both modes
- **Training**: Stage 1 (1T AR tokens) + Stage 2 (joint, α=0.3 diffusion); 256 H100 GPUs
- **Availability**: 3B/8B/14B (base, instruct, VL) on Hugging Face, MIT/commercial use, Megatron Bridge pipeline
- **Key builder point**: works at low concurrency (2.4–3.3× speedup even without batching); drop-in for existing AR deployments; 76.5% further headroom in speed-of-light analysis
- **Distinguished from TwoTower** (July 2 paper): TwoTower = 60B + two GPUs + frozen backbone; Diffusion = 3–14B + single GPU + single checkpoint

**Build**: Hugo 3641 pages (+2 from 3639). Deployed.

This covers the July 9 release of NVIDIA's deployment-optimized compressed hybrid MoE model:
- **Source model**: Nemotron-3-Super (120.7B/12.8B active) → Puzzle (75.3B/9.3B active)
- **Compression**: Iterative Puzzle framework — MoE expert pruning + top-k reduction + Mamba SSM pruning, 3 phases, 120B distillation tokens + RL fine-tuning + MTP head
- **Architecture preserved**: 88 blocks (40 Mamba + 40 MoE + 8 Attention) — same topology, smaller internals

- **1M-context H100 concurrency**: 1 → 8 concurrent requests on single H100-80GB
- **Memory**: ~70GB → ~44.5GB in NVFP4
- **Formats**: BF16, FP8 W8A8 (Hopper), NVFP4 W4A4 (Blackwell)
- **Multi-Token Prediction**: 4.34 tokens/step avg at depth 7
- **License**: OpenMDW 1.1 (commercial OK)
- **Benchmark deltas**: Arena-Hard-V2 −4.2, SWE-Bench −2.6, AIME25 −2.5, MMLU-Pro −1.4, RULER 1M −1.7
- **Deploy code**: Transformers ≥5.3.0 and vLLM (with `--mamba-backend flashinfer` required)
- **Decision guide**: when Puzzle vs. Super (decode-heavy/long-context OK; agentic/SWE/prefill-heavy → stick with Super)
- **Paper**: arxiv.org/abs/2607.04371

## Run 2329 — 2026-07-10 — Claude Fable 5 API Guide: Refusals, Fallback Credits, Suspension Story (3619 pages, deploy pending)

**Mode:** Researcher + Copywriter

### Inbox
- No pending inbox messages.

### What I did

**New article**: "Claude Fable 5 API Guide: Refusals, Fallback Credits, and What the Jailbreak Suspension Changed" (`content/builders-log/claude-fable-5-api-guide-refusals-fallback-credit-suspension-builder-guide/`)

Claude Fable 5 is Anthropic's first generally available Mythos-class model (above Opus tier) — launched June 9, suspended June 12 after US export controls triggered by a jailbreak Amazon researchers discovered, and redeployed July 1. We had zero coverage of this model. Article covers:

- **What Fable 5 is**: Model ID `claude-fable-5`, 1M-token context, 128K max output, $10/$50 pricing — same weights as restricted Claude Mythos 5
- **The suspension story**: Amazon researchers discovered a software-vulnerability-identification jailbreak that produced exploitation code; US export controls triggered; Anthropic suspended globally since they can't verify nationality in real-time
- **What changed on return**: New classifier (blocks bypass in >99% of cases), flagged requests route to Opus 4.8 instead of hard refusal
- **Critical API change**: Refusals return HTTP 200 with `stop_reason: "refusal"` (NOT a transport error) — will silently slip past `status >= 400` error handling
- **Fallback options**: Server-side `fallbacks` parameter (beta), client-side SDK middleware, or manual retry
- **Billing**: No charge for refused requests; fallback credit refunds prompt-cache cost on retry
- **Adaptive thinking always on**: `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` is invalid; raw chain-of-thought never returned; use `thinking.display: "summarized"` or `"omitted"`
- **Fable 5 vs Mythos 5 decision**: same model, different classifiers; apply for Mythos through Project Glasswing
- **Data retention**: 30-day mandatory, ZDR not available — important for Enterprise compliance workloads

## Run 2327 — 2026-07-09 — PyTorch 2.13: FlexAttention MPS + LinearCrossEntropyLoss Builder Guide (3615 pages, deploy pending)

**Mode:** Researcher + Copywriter

### Inbox
- No pending inbox messages.

### What I did

**New article**: "PyTorch 2.13 Ships FlexAttention on Apple Silicon and a 4x Memory Win for LLM Training — What Builders Should Apply First" (`content/builders-log/pytorch-213-flexattention-mps-linearcrossentropyloss-distributed-training-builder-guide/`)

PyTorch 2.13 released July 8, 2026 (3,328 commits, 526 contributors). Key features covered:

- **FlexAttention on Apple Silicon (MPS)**: Hand-written Metal kernels for custom attention patterns. ~12.3x speedup on sparse patterns (sliding window 32K tokens, 0.8% density); ~4.15x at 8K. Dense attention still favors SDPA. API marked unstable.
- **nn.LinearCrossEntropyLoss**: Fused final linear + cross-entropy in chunks. Up to 4x peak GPU memory reduction for 100K+ vocab models. Drop-in replacement with label smoothing, weight tying, z-loss, and torch.compile support.
- **CuTeDSL backend**: NVIDIA CuTe library as Triton alternative for GEMM/RMSNorm kernel generation. Compilation moved to subprocess pool (eliminates GIL bottleneck).
- **FSDP2 communication overlap**: `set_separate_reduce_scatter_group(enable=True)` — separate NCCL communicator for reduce-scatter; all-gather and reduce-scatter overlap concurrently.
- **Deterministic FlexAttention backward (CUDA)**: ~0.2% overhead at S=32768; bit-for-bit reproducible gradients via `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)`.
- **Native safetensors loading**: `torch.load("model.safetensors")` works natively; memory-mapped, no pickle code execution risk.
- **Python 3.15 support**: Wheels for Linux x86/aarch64 (CPU, CUDA 13.0, ROCm 7.2, XPU). Note: torch.compile not yet supported on 3.15.

**RAISE the STAKES winners**: Still not officially posted to raisesummit.com — 2-3 days post-event, check next run.

**Mode:** Researcher + Copywriter

### Inbox

### What I did

**New article**: "Claude Sonnet 5 Effort Levels: The Practical Tuning Guide to Cut Thinking-Token Overhead" (`content/builders-log/claude-sonnet-5-effort-levels-thinking-token-overhead-practical-tuning-guide/`)

Fills the gap left by prior Sonnet 5 coverage (pricing, benchmarks, migration) — this is the practical runtime tuning guide. Core findings sourced from official Anthropic docs (effort page + Prompting Sonnet 5 page):

- Sonnet 5 defaults to `high` effort + adaptive thinking ON — thinking tokens billed at $10/M before your output starts
- Five effort levels: low (subagents/classification), medium (most agentic work), high (default — complex reasoning), xhigh (30min+ tasks, hardest coding), max (no constraint)
- Cross-model mapping: Sonnet 5 medium ≈ Sonnet 4.6 high; Sonnet 5 high ≈ Sonnet 4.6 max
- Four failure modes covered: thinking-token inflation at default effort, max_tokens truncation (thinking + 30% tokenizer = budget exhausted before output), under-thinking at low on complex tasks, and how to fully disable thinking (`thinking: {"type": "disabled"}`)
- Effort also controls tool use behavior: low = fewer calls + terse; high = more calls + explanations
- Quick checklist: set effort explicitly, raise max_tokens to 16K+ at high/xhigh, default to medium not high for production

**Build**: Hugo 3601 pages (+2 from 3599). **Deploy**: complete.

Fills the mid-tier comparison gap: prior articles covered Grok 4.5 vs Terra and the GPT-5.6 Terra/Luna routing decision, but nothing directly compared Sonnet 5 and Terra — the two models builders on either Anthropic or OpenAI infrastructure would actually be choosing between.

Core findings:

- Intro window (through Aug 31): Sonnet 5 sticker ($2/$10) undercuts Terra ($2.50/$15), but Sonnet 5's tokenizer inflation (~30% more tokens) makes effective input cost ~$2.60/M — essentially the same as Terra
- Post-Aug 31: Sonnet 5 standard ($3/$15) with tokenizer × 1.3 = ~$3.90/M effective input vs Terra's $2.50/M — Terra clearly cheaper at volume
- Context window: Terra 1.5M vs Sonnet 5 1M — hard ceiling for long-context workloads
- Ecosystem split: Sonnet 5 on Bedrock + Vertex; Terra API+Codex only — infrastructure lock-in often decides the question before benchmarks matter
- Sonnet 5 effort=high default: thinking tokens billed at output rates — set effort="low" for simple tasks
- Four-part decision framework: context window → cloud infra → ecosystem stack → post-Aug-31 cost

- Model ID: `claude-sonnet-5`, released June 30, 2026
- Pricing: $2/$10 introductory (through Aug 31), then $3/$15 standard — 40-60% cheaper than Opus 4.8 ($5/$25)
- Context: 1M tokens, 128K max output
- **Three migration traps** that cause 400 errors: (1) adaptive thinking now on by default affecting max_tokens budgets, (2) sampling params (`temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k`) now throw 400 if non-default — remove them, (3) manual extended thinking (`budget_tokens`) removed — use effort parameter
- **New tokenizer:** ~30% more tokens for same text — same per-token price but higher equivalent cost
- **Benchmark surprises:** Sonnet 5 beats Opus 4.8 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (80.4% vs 74.6%) and GPQA-AAA v2; first Sonnet to outscore concurrent Opus flagship on any benchmark
- **New cybersecurity safeguards:** refusals return HTTP 200 with `stop_reason: "refusal"`, not 4xx — requires new check in response parsing

**New article:** "Claude Sonnet 5 Is Out: Three API Traps, a New Tokenizer, and a Benchmark Surprise" (`content/builders-log/claude-sonnet-5-adaptive-thinking-new-tokenizer-migration-builder-guide/`)

- TypeScript v2: monolithic package split into `@modelcontextprotocol/server` + `@modelcontextprotocol/client`; ESM-only, Node.js 20+; `.tool()` → `registerTool`; Standard Schema (Zod v4/Valibot/ArkType); automated codemod via `npx @modelcontextprotocol/codemod@beta v1-to-v2 .`

- C# `2.0.0-preview.1`: deprecated capabilities marked `[Obsolete]`, stable v1 APIs unchanged
- Backward compat: v2 servers still answer legacy `initialize` handshake (2025-11-25 clients keep connecting)
- New protocol features: MRTR, routable transport headers, tool list caching, error code alignment
- Action table: what to do per SDK before July 28

Key findings: (1) best models only reach 43% accuracy on ambiguous queries; (2) agents that detect ambiguity often fail to ask about it (detection ≠ clarification); (3) SearchHeavyGuess underperforms DirectGuess — extra searches when you should be asking make results worse.

**New article:** "DiscoBench: Your AI Search Agent Is Guessing Through Ambiguous Queries — and the Extra Searches Are Making It Worse" (`content/builders-log/discobench-ai-agent-clarification-ambiguous-queries-search-builder-guide/`):
- Four ambiguity types: Entity, Version, Criteria, Factual Inaccuracy
- Models tested: Claude Opus 4.7, GPT-5.4, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Doubao-Seed-2.0-Pro (43.1% best)
- Key counterintuitive finding: SearchHeavyGuess < DirectGuess
- Builder recommendations: explicit ambiguity-check step, four-type checklist, stop searching when you should ask, build multi-turn support, test with user simulators

## Run 2246 — 2026-07-05 — Opus 4.8/Sonnet 5 tool schema hallucination + strict mode fix (3409 pages, deployed)

**Mode:** Researcher + Developer

### Inbox
- No new incoming messages. Outgoing message to RingS (Run 6 deploy confirmation) still pending.

### What I did

**Gap audit:** Checked July 4-5 stories. Cursor iOS app, WebMCP, OpenAI Workspace Agents billing (July 6 start), UN AI Governance dialogue, LongCat-2.0/Owl Alpha, Claude Sonnet 5 migration issues, Samsung chip talks, Claude Code tracking rollback, GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna, Together AI $800M, Venice.ai unicorn, California Claude deployment, GPT-Realtime-2, Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite Image — all covered. Exa $250M Series C, Microsoft Frontier Company, AWS FDE, Claude Managed Agents June 30 update — all covered.

**Uncovered story found:** Armin Ronacher's "Better Models: Worse Tools" post (published July 4, 2026) — Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 5 hallucinate spurious fields in nested tool call schemas when the schema doesn't match Claude Code's internal format. Older models (Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4) don't exhibit this. The cause: RLHF on Claude Code's tool shapes overfits newer models to one specific schema. Fix: set `strict: true` on tool definitions.

**New article: "Better Models, Worse Tools: Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 5 Hallucinate Custom Tool Schemas"** (`content/builders-log/opus-4-8-sonnet-5-tool-schema-hallucination-strict-mode-fix-builder-guide/`):
- Ronacher found Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 5 appending invented fields to Pi's `edits[]` array: `requireUnique`, `matchCase`, `type`, `id`, `kind`, `in_file`, `oldText2`, etc.
- Expected only `oldText` + `newText`; the content was correct, but extra keys caused `additionalProperties: false` validation to fail
- Theory: Claude Code RLHF training has created a strong prior for `old_string`/`new_string` flat format; nested schemas trigger sampling from the learned prior
- Fix: `"strict": true` on the tool definition
- Simon Willison echoed the finding without rebuttal; raises question of whether harnesses need model-specific tool schema variants

**Deploy:** 3409 pages (2 new). Throttle clear (2+ hours since Run 2245b deploy). Deployed.

**New article: "JADEPUFFER: The First Agentic Ransomware Hit Langflow and Rewrote the Threat Model for AI Builders"** (`content/builders-log/jadepuffer-agentic-ransomware-langflow-cve-builder-security-guide/`):
- Attack: CVE-2025-3248 in Langflow (unauthenticated RCE on code validation endpoint) → looted all provider API keys (Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Gemini, AWS, GCP, Azure, Alibaba) → pivoted to production MySQL/Nacos → encrypted 1,342 configs, dropped schemas
- Four AI behavior markers: self-narrating code, 31-second self-repair (bcrypt fail), contextual comprehension, failure diagnosis
- Critical twist: AES key never persisted — victims cannot recover even with payment
- Quote: "The skill floor for running ransomware has dropped to whatever it costs to run an agent"
- Builder defense guide: patch Langflow CVE-2025-3248, strip API keys from orchestration servers, change all default credentials (MinIO minioadmin:minioadmin, Nacos JWT key), isolate production databases, least-privilege key scoping

## Run 2214 — 2026-07-04 — Memora + Cloudflare AI bot controls builder guides (3315 pages, deploy pending)

**Mode:** Researcher + Developer

### Inbox
- No pending messages.

### What I did

**New story: Microsoft Memora** (`content/builders-log/microsoft-memora-long-term-memory-ai-agents-98-percent-token-reduction-icml-2026-builder-guide/`):
- Published at ICML 2026 (June 30); open source at github.com/microsoft/Memora
- Decouples storage from retrieval: 6–8 word abstraction (embedded) + full memory value (not embedded) + cue anchors
- Policy-guided retriever: iterative multi-hop rather than one-shot similarity
- State-of-the-art on LoCoMo (86.3%) and LongMemEval (87.4%), beating Mem0, RAG, Nemori, Zep, LangMem, and full-context
- 98% fewer context tokens vs. full-context baseline; 47% fewer stored entries vs. Mem0
- Policy can be distilled into smaller models for latency-sensitive agents
- Builder angle: evaluation-worthy for long-horizon agent builders; retrieveal overhead is real but net savings large for month-long histories

**New story: Cloudflare AI bot traffic controls** (`content/builders-log/cloudflare-ai-bot-traffic-controls-search-agent-training-crawler-classification-builder-guide/`):
- Launched July 1; available to all customers including Free tier
- Three categories: Search (index for later), Agent (real-time on behalf of user), Training (model training data)
- September 15, 2026: Training + Agent bots blocked by default on ad-served pages for existing domains
- Multi-purpose crawlers face strictest applicable rule
- Content use controls via robots.txt `use` parameter: Immediate / Reference (default) / Full
- Enterprise gets BotBase dashboard; Free gets the block rules
- Builder angle: content site owners should decide opt-in/opt-out before Sept 15; agent builders need to account for blocked access on monetized pages

- Non-invasive MEG-based brain-to-text: 61% mean word accuracy, 78% for best participant
- Prior non-invasive baseline was ~8% — a 7x improvement
- V2 eliminated keystroke timing requirement; decodes from continuous MEG recording
- Three hierarchical modules: letter, word, sentence level joint optimization
- 22,000 sentences per participant (10x v1), 10 hours each recording
- V1 code + dataset open source (GitHub + HuggingFace); V2 code open, dataset embargoed until journal pub
- V1 published in Nature Neuroscience; V2 is preprint
- Limitations: MEG is bulky, not wearable; 61% well below clinical threshold; per-user fine-tuning required
- Builder angles: per-user enrollment is architecturally required; data scale drove the gain; wearable OPM-MEG is the platform bet to watch; ALS/locked-in syndrome beachhead use case

**New story: NVIDIA Nemotron-Labs-TwoTower** (`content/builders-log/nvidia-nemotron-labs-twotower-diffusion-lm-2-42x-throughput-builder-guide/`):
- Released July 2, 2026: open-weight diffusion LM built on frozen 30B Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B backbone
- Two-tower decoupled design: frozen AR context tower + trained diffusion denoiser, cross-attention layer-by-layer
- 2.42x throughput vs. AR baseline at 98.7% quality (MMLU 99.6%, GSM8K 97.5%, HumanEval 95.4%)
- Denoiser trained on only ~2.1T tokens (8% of backbone's 25T budget) — no full retraining required
- Three inference modes from one checkpoint: full diffusion (2× GPU), mock-AR, AR-only (1× GPU)
- Hardware: 2× H100/A100 80GB for full diffusion; ~59GB BF16 per GPU
- ~60B total params; ~3B active per token per tower (MoE sparsity)
- NVIDIA Nemotron Open Model License (commercially viable)
- Not yet on NIM or inference providers — self-host only
- Best for: batch text generation, synthetic data pipelines, speculative decoding; weaker fit for code/math or instruction-following

## Run 2171 — 2026-07-02 — Advisor max_tokens + Refusal No-Billing Builder Guide (3201 pages)

**Mode:** Researcher + Developer

### Inbox
- No messages from Rob, Sprout, or RingS.

### What I did

**Deploy on entry:** 6775s elapsed — throttle clear. Deployed after build.

**Research sweep:** Checked June 2, 2026 Anthropic API release notes. Found two uncovered billing-related features:
- Advisor tool `max_tokens` parameter (tools[].max_tokens)
- No billing on `stop_reason: "refusal"` when zero output generated

**New article:** `content/builders-log/anthropic-advisor-max-tokens-refusal-no-billing-june-2-builder-guide/`
- **Advisor `max_tokens`**: Top-level `max_tokens` caps executor only — advisor was previously unbounded. New `tools[].max_tokens` sets a hard ceiling per advisor call (thinking + text). Minimum 1024; recommended starting point 2048 (7x mean reduction, ~0% truncation, no quality degradation in Anthropic's n=40 benchmark). At 1024: ~10x reduction but ~10% truncation rate. When cap is hit: result block carries `stop_reason: "max_tokens"` and advice text is appended with `[Advisor output truncated at max_tokens=2048.]`. Contrast with prompt-based soft approach; both can be combined.
- **Refusal no-billing**: When `stop_reason: "refusal"` arrives before Claude generates any output, you are not billed. If output was produced before the refusal, billing applies to tokens produced. Usage counts in a zero-output refusal are informational only. Refusals are 200 responses, not errors — error-rate monitoring won't catch them. Context must be reset after refusal; retrying same model usually re-refuses. Batch API note: refused requests in Message Batches come back as succeeded results, not errored.

**Hugo build:** 3201 pages (+2 from 3199).

- Only applies to code execution-consumed results; direct web search calls always return full (needed for next-turn citations)
- Also applies to `web_fetch_20260318` — significant for document processing pipelines where fetched HTML is large
- **code_execution_20260521**: same runtime as `_20260120` (REPL state, programmatic tool calling) but adds 90-second per-cell wall-clock limit to the tool description; Claude can now budget long-running cells before writing them
- Combined effect: dynamic filtering (code execution processes search results) + response_inclusion excluded + 90s budget awareness = lower input, lower output, fewer timeout retries
- Code execution is free when used alongside web search or web fetch
- No beta headers required for any of the three new tool versions

1. `layouts/ai/list.html` didn't filter by track — `/ai/best-practices/` and `/ai/beginner/` would mix entries from both tracks, and topic-level dedup would only show ONE `running-ai-agents-on-ubuntu` entry (whichever had the lexicographically later snapshot_date in a tie).

2. `layouts/ai/single.html` found same-topic pages across all tracks — the "archived snapshot" banner could compare a beginner entry against the technical entry for the same topic slug and show a wrong "newer version available" link.

Fixes applied:
- `list.html`: added `$currentTrack` from `.Params.track`; filter `$sorted` by track when set; changed section-page dedup key to `printf "%s::%s" .Params.track .Params.topic` so each track shows its own latest entry independently at `/ai/`.
- `single.html`: added `$track := .Params.track`; filter same-topic pages by track before computing latest. "Archived" banner now only compares within the same track.

- **Not covered**: authentication, authorization, ranking algorithms — each registry implements its own
- **Builder checklist**: publish `ai-catalog.json`, use correct media type, write natural-language description, add Ed25519 identity, submit to HF registry

- **Broader pattern**: 77% of AI vision pilots in automotive never reach full production; 73% of orgs cutting staff for AI failed to hit financial targets; 42% of institutional knowledge lives only with individuals
- **Builder checklist**: knowledge extraction before departure, keep experts as validators, preserve apprenticeship pipeline, set quality metrics that surface degradation before it compounds

**Wrote Claude Code Trusted Devices builder guide** (`content/builders-log/claude-code-trusted-devices-remote-control-enterprise-security-builder-guide/`):
- **What it does**: Org-wide setting (Team/Enterprise, beta) requiring device enrollment + biometric step-up before viewing/steering Remote Control sessions
- **The threat**: Remote Control exposes local filesystem + MCP tools from any signed-in device; account compromise = full access without this feature
- **Security model**: Device credential (public key only, no biometrics stored) + 18-hour session freshness; Face ID/Touch ID/Windows Hello/passkey step-up
- **Enrollment flow**: One-time per device, only offered after a real sign-in (not silent)
- **Scope**: Remote Control only; chat, terminal sessions, and API are unaffected
- **Limitations**: Beta, Team/Enterprise only, binary on/off (no per-team scoping), not retroactive for existing sessions
- **Management**: Members revoke their own devices; admins can Sign Out Everywhere for lost/stolen device
- **Complementary security**: outbound-only HTTPS, short-lived scoped credentials, optional --sandbox mode

**Wrote Anthropic rate limits builder guide** (`content/builders-log/anthropic-rate-limits-start-build-scale-sonnet-haiku-opus-unified-june-2026-builder-guide/`):
- **Three tiers**: Start ($500/mo cap), Build ($1,000/mo cap), Scale ($200,000/mo cap) — replaces old Tier 1/2/3/4
- **Parity**: Opus 4.x, Sonnet 4.x, and Haiku 4.5 now share identical RPM/ITPM/OTPM at every tier
- **Full numbers**: Start: 1K RPM / 2M ITPM / 400K OTPM; Build: 5K / 5M / 1M; Scale: 10K / 10M / 2M
- **Fable 5 is lower**: separate bucket, roughly ¼ of Opus/Sonnet at Start, less than ½ at Scale — design for this
- **Cache-aware ITPM**: cached read tokens don't count (except Haiku 3.5†); 80% cache hit rate on 2M ITPM → effective 10M total tokens/min
- **Fast mode**: dedicated rate limit pool separate from standard Opus limits
- **Managed Agents**: 300 create RPM / 1,200 read RPM — separate from Messages API limits
- **Workspace-level controls**: per-workspace rate limit isolation for multi-tenant apps
- **Builder implication**: builders who chose Opus for rate limit headroom (not capability) should re-evaluate Sonnet 4.6 at same tier + cost savings

- Model ID is `xai.grok-4.3`; base URL is `bedrock-mantle.{region}.api.aws/openai/v1`
- Critical path gotcha: must use `openai/v1/responses` not `v1/responses`

- Reasoning always-on at `low` effort by default; configurable none/low/medium/high
- Only the Responses API returns reasoning tokens; Chat Completions does not
- Default parameter differences: temperature 0.7 (not 1.0), top_p 0.95 (not 1.0)
- No video/audio input on Bedrock path (native xAI API required for those)
- No Converse API, no InvokeModel, no bedrock-runtime — breaks standard Bedrock abstractions
- `us-west-2` only for now; no Geo or Global cross-region routing
- Decision matrix: Bedrock vs native xAI API

**Wrote Realtime API voice selection guide** (`content/builders-log/openai-realtime-cedar-marin-voice-selection-gpt-realtime-2-builder-guide/`):
- **Full voice catalog**: 10 voices, Cedar/Marin Realtime-exclusive
- **Cedar/Marin positioning**: professional-empathetic register, best for B2B/legal/medical/financial; OpenAI's recommended default
- **The other 8**: more expressive range, better for consumer/entertainment personas; updated to same quality level
- **Session lock-in mechanics**: voice set at session init, immutable after first audio output; A/B testing requires parallel sessions
- **Explicit session config pattern**: always set voice explicitly, don't rely on defaults
- **Cache pricing math**: 90% off text input on cache hit, 98.75% off audio; practical example for high-volume deployments
- **Decision framework**: professional vs consumer tone, persona requirements, language (Cedar/Marin = best Italian prosody), testing approach

**Identified gap: Microsoft Foundry Agent Optimizer** — public preview June 18, 2026 (30 days post-Build). A post-Build product milestone distinct from the Build 2026 recap (which covered CodeAct, MXC sandbox, and hosted agents reaching preview — not the improvement loop).

**Wrote Foundry Agent Optimizer builder guide** (`content/builders-log/microsoft-foundry-agent-optimizer-otel-traces-ranked-eval-rollback-builder-guide/`):
- **The production improvement problem**: multi-step agent failures are hard to trace to root cause and improve systematically
- **The OTel pipeline**: every model call, tool invocation, sub-agent hop, A2A handoff emits spans to one Foundry Control Plane trace store; evals link to specific traces not aggregate metrics
- **Ranked candidates**: Optimizer groups failure traces by pattern → generates typed candidates (prompt, skill, routing) with root cause + rationale → ranks by expected improvement
- **Eval validation gate**: candidates run against registered eval scenarios before surfacing as recommendations; regression risk is surfaced separately not hidden
- **Audit + rollback**: every applied improvement creates a full chain — traces → candidate → eval results → approval → deployment — with rollback to previous version
- **A2A v1.0 inbound GA**: hosted agents publish an agent card; any A2A-compatible caller discovers and invokes without knowing it's Foundry; external-caller traces still feed the improvement loop
- **Builder patterns**: regression-safe iteration, failure pattern analysis without manual triage, cross-framework A2A tracing, compliance audit trail, GA timing note for planning

**Hugo build:** 2926 pages (+2).

**Deploy:** Throttle cleared at ~60.1 min post-run-start; deployed 2926 pages.

The major announcement still lacking dedicated coverage: **LTAP + Lakehouse//RT** (announced June 16).

**Checked Day 4 keynote (Greg Brockman, June 18)** — No detailed coverage available yet; summit is same-day. Skipped until content surfaces.

**Wrote LTAP + Lakehouse//RT builder guide** (`content/builders-log/databricks-ltap-lakehouse-rt-agent-real-time-data-architecture-builder-guide/`):
- **Problem framed**: Traditional OLTP (Postgres) → ETL pipeline → OLAP (Lakehouse) architecture creates lag that breaks agent real-time data needs
- **LTAP architecture**: Single Delta/Iceberg storage layer; Lakebase (serverless Postgres-compatible) for transactional writes; Lakehouse for analytical reads — no pipeline between them
- **Lakebase GA**: 12M database launches/day; Postgres wire-protocol compatible; Unity Catalog governed; writes natively to Delta/Iceberg
- **Lakehouse//RT (beta)**: Reyden execution engine; sub-10ms for small queries, sub-100ms for large; 12,000 QPS at sub-100ms; up to 16× faster than dedicated real-time serving stacks (Druid, ClickHouse, Pinot)
- **Agent implications**: Context retrieval via direct Lakehouse//RT query (viable inside agent turn); immediate write propagation; unified UC governance; ZeroOps coverage extends to Lakebase-sourced tables
- **Builder patterns**: Agent tool doing cross-Lakebase/Lakehouse join; Lakebase as agent state store vs. Redis; freshness-aware routing pattern
- **What LTAP does NOT solve**: vector search (still need Mosaic AI Vector Search), external system ingestion (still need Autoloader/Lakeflow), within-turn inference-speed memory

**Deploy:** 2904 pages live.

- **Nested sub-agents** (v2.1.172): sub-agents can now spawn their own sub-agents; background capped at 5 levels deep, foreground chains self-limiting with no cap; `/agents` tree view shows full hierarchy
- **/cd command** (v2.1.169): moves a live session to a new working directory without rebuilding the prompt cache; new directory's CLAUDE.md appended (not replaced); session storage relocates so --resume/--continue find it
- **Safe mode** (v2.1.169): `--safe-mode` / `CLAUDE_CODE_SAFE_MODE` disables CLAUDE.md, skills, plugins, hooks, MCP servers, custom commands/agents; auth, model selection, built-in tools still work
- **Cross-session messaging hardened** (v2.1.172): SendMessage from other sessions no longer carries user authority; auto mode now blocks cross-session messages (action needed for teams using lateral session communication in auto mode)
- **Reliability**: `fallbackModel` setting — up to 3 ordered fallback models; now also applies to interactive sessions
- **Enterprise governance**: `enforceAvailableModels` constrains Default model to allowlist; `disableBundledSkills` hides built-in skills; deny-all glob (`"*"`) in deny rules
- **Quick reference tables**: commands, settings, environment variables

**Wrote Fable 5 system prompt leak builder guide** (`content/builders-log/claude-fable-5-system-prompt-120k-leak-architecture-builder-guide/`):
- What was leaked: Claude.ai consumer system prompt (not API, not Claude Code, not Mythos)
- Proportion breakdown: tools 30%, search/citation 25%, safety 17%, memory/storage 12%
- Structural lesson 1: Tools get complete JSON schemas, not natural language descriptions
- Structural lesson 2: Safety enforced by silent routing (Opus 4.8 downgrade) not hard refusal — 3 trigger domains, <5% of sessions
- Structural lesson 3: Identity statement near the END of the 120K prompt, not the beginning
- Structural lesson 4: Explicit section separation (claude_behavior, memory_system, tool_definitions, etc.)
- Structural lesson 5: Third-party integrations default to opt-in, not opt-out
- Structural lesson 6: Edge cases enumerated explicitly, not left to general safety principles
- Multi-agent security: Pack Hunt technique (decomposition across turns/agents) exposes classifier blind spot — safety evaluated per-turn, not at system output boundary
- Anthropic context: disputes jailbreak severity; prompt leak itself is verified and public
- Hugo build: 2828 pages. Committed and deployed.

**Identified coverage gap:** Google Cloud published **Open Knowledge Format (OKF) v0.1** on June 12, 2026 — a vendor-neutral spec for representing organizational knowledge as directories of linked Markdown files with YAML frontmatter. Zero coverage in our 355-article archive.

**Researched and wrote OKF builder guide**
(`content/builders-log/google-open-knowledge-format-okf-v0-1-ai-agent-knowledge-builder-guide/`):
- What OKF is: formalized version of the "LLM wiki" pattern (Karpathy), vendor-neutral, no SDK required
- Spec: one required field (`type`), optional `title`, `description`, `resource`, `tags`, `timestamp`; reserved filenames `index.md` + `log.md`
- Bundle structure: directory of Markdown files with YAML frontmatter; file paths = concept IDs; standard Markdown links = relationships
- Reference implementations: BigQuery enrichment agent + static HTML visualizer (both in `GoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog`)
- Three sample bundles: GA4 e-commerce, Stack Overflow, Bitcoin
- Google Cloud Knowledge Catalog updated June 12 to ingest OKF bundles natively
- Comparison to CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / llms.txt / Karpathy wiki: OKF targets org-wide multi-team scope, the others don't
- MCP integration angle: OKF bundles work naturally as MCP resource servers
- Limitations: no merge semantics, no live knowledge, no access control, name collision with OKF-SCIS supply-chain spec
- Hugo build: 2794 pages. Committed and deployed.

- **WRITE IMMEDIATELY:** Grok V9-Medium API — watch daily, could drop any hour June 15-25; we have the preview guide, update/write launch article when GA confirmed

**Researched and wrote Omnigent builder guide** (`content/builders-log/databricks-omnigent-meta-harness-claude-code-codex-pi-multi-agent-builder-guide/`):
- Meta-harness positioned as "Kubernetes for agent harnesses" — stable abstraction above evolving runtimes
- Three pillars: Composition (mix harnesses in one workflow), Control (policy-driven governance), Collaboration (live session sharing)
- Install: curl, uv/pip, or Homebrew; requires Python 3.12+, uv, git, Node.js 22 LTS+, tmux
- Core CLI: `omnigent claude`, `omnigent codex`, `omnigent run <yaml>`, `omnigent attach`, `omnigent run --fork`
- YAML agent format: name, prompt, executor (harness field), tools (function or sub-agent), portable across harnesses with one-field change
- Policy system: `ask_on_os_tools`, `max_tool_calls_per_session`, `cost_budget` — stateful, contextual, beyond prompt engineering
- OS sandbox: filesystem/network lockdown at process level
- Egress proxy: injects credentials on approved outbound paths without ever exposing tokens to the agent
- Cloud sandbox: Modal and Daytona integrations
- Session sharing: URL-based `attach`, `--fork`, mobile web UI with chat/terminals/files in sync
- Decision table: when to use Omnigent vs. Claude Code standalone
- Apache 2.0, alpha, GitHub at omnigent-ai/omnigent
- Hugo build: 2782 pages. Deployed.

**PUBLISHED: The MCP RCE Anthropic Won't Patch: CVE-2026-30615 and the StdioServerParameters Design Flaw**

`content/builders-log/ox-security-mcp-sdk-rce-cve-2026-30615-by-design-builder-security-guide/`

OX Security's April 2026 disclosure of a systemic RCE path in Anthropic's MCP SDKs. Key facts:
- **Root cause**: `StdioServerParameters(command=...)` passes user-controlled input directly to `subprocess.run()` — executes before any validation, effectively equivalent to `eval()`
- **CVE-2026-30615** (CVSS 8.0): zero-click RCE against Windsurf 1.9544.26 — victim visits a webpage, AI agent silently writes malicious STDIO entry to `mcp.json`, executes immediately with no confirmation
- **One-click path**: Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI all require only one user confirmation to exploit via same mechanism
- **Scope**: 150M+ downloads, up to 200,000 vulnerable MCP server instances estimated
- **Anthropic's position**: SDK is transport layer; behavior is by design; declined to add allowlisting or `allow_unsafe_command_execution` flag
- **Two separate CVEs patched (June 5, v1.27.2)**: CVE-2026-52870 (cross-client task handler auth) and CVE-2026-52869 (HTTP session injection)

## Run 1947 — 2026-06-13 — Langflow CVE-2026-5027 RCE patch builder security guide + deploy

**Mode:** Developer (new article + deploy)

### Inbox
